feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start = the dedication of the Main Injector (see its operating interval); ring commissioning began in September 1998. 8 GeV protons into the Main Injector (the Tevatron-era chain: "Protons from the Booster and antiprotons from the Recycler were accelerated to 150 GeV in the Main Injector").
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: This accelerator would use the Fermilab 8 GeV Booster as an injector and have the ability to accelerate protons up to 150 GeV

feeds_accelerator_ids.locator: Fermilab proton complex status, arXiv:1705.03075, section on the Recycler
feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start as on the Recycler's proton-stacking interval: "just 6 batches in late 2014" is the first documented step and the Recycler was an antiproton ring until the Tevatron stopped in 2011. Proton beam studies in the Recycler during commissioning (1999 to 2004) are not counted as chain operation.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: the Recycler is now used to stack high intensity protons for loading into the 120 GeV Main Injector synchrotron which is located in the same tunnel. Circumference of the Recycler is sufficient to accommodate six batches of 84 Booster bunches each;

start.display: by late 2014 (first documented step: 6 batches stacked); not before the Tevatron stopped in 2011

intervals.label: commissioning after completion of construction
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Booster'
intervals.note: Start is the completion of construction (21 December 1970); the end is the day the Booster reached its design energy of 8 GeV (21 May 1971), after which it is recorded as operating. No source fetched gives a groundbreaking date for the ring, so no construction interval is written.
intervals.quote: The lab completed construction of the Booster on December 21, 1970.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.locator: Fermilab History and Archives, page 'Accelerator History', section 'Booster'
intervals.note: Start is the day the Booster achieved its design energy of 8 GeV (21 May 1971). NuMI beam data taking from 20 May 2005 (NuMI beam paper) documents it as operating in the neutrino era.
intervals.quote: The Booster achieved its design energy of 8 GeV on May 21, 1971.

end.display: between Run Ia (ended May 1993) and Run Ib (began December 1993)

intervals.label: 200 MeV injection (before the 1993 Linac upgrade)
intervals.locator: Shiltsev, arXiv:1109.1864, section on Run I
intervals.note: The Linac upgrade from the initial 200 MeV to 400 MeV aimed at reducing space-charge effects at the Booster's injection energy; end as on accelerator:fermilab-linac.
intervals.quote: The 400 MeV linac upgrade (from the initial 200 MeV) was implemented between Run Ia and Run Ib

injection_energy.locator: Shiltsev, arXiv:1109.1864, section on Run I
injection_energy.quote: The 400 MeV linac upgrade (from the initial 200 MeV) was implemented between Run Ia and Run Ib

intervals.label: Injection from the PIP-II linac (planned)
intervals.locator: IPAC'26 talk (M. Convery, 19 May 2026), slide "Accelerator program evolution"
intervals.note: Schedule value, not an event: after the 2028-2029 "long shutdown" the Booster is commissioned with beam from the PIP-II linac, and "Operation of LBNF beam to DUNE will begin in 2031" (same slide). The 800 MeV injection energy is in the talk's table "Key parameters" (Linac 400, Linac2 800 MeV).
intervals.quote: Booster commissioning with beam from the PIP-II linac uses the Booster Neutrino Beam facility which allows an experimental program if approved

injection_energy.locator: IPAC'26 talk, slide "PIP-II project and Linac2"
injection_energy.note: Design value of the PIP-II linac; planned, not yet in operation.
injection_energy.quote: Linac2 is an 800 MeV H- superconducting RF linac, compatible with CW operations and upgradeable to 1 GeV

start.display: after the 2028-2029 long shutdown; LBNF beam to DUNE planned for 2031

beam_energy.locator: §4.2 NuMI Mode of Operation; arXiv PDF p. 50
beam_energy.quote: The Booster then accelerates those protons to 8 GeV.

circumference.quote: The FNAL Booster is a 474-meter-circumference synchrotron operating at 15Hz.

injection_energy.locator: NuMI Neutrino Beam paper, §2; IPAC'26 talk, table "Key parameters"
injection_energy.note: Current Linac injection energy (H- ions, stripped to protons in the Booster). 200 MeV before the 1993 Linac upgrade; 800 MeV planned with the PIP-II linac (see the intervals).
injection_energy.quote: Protons originate as H− ions in the Linac which accelerates them to 400 MeV. The ions are converted into protons in the Booster where they are accelerated to 8 GeV as 1.6 µs long batches with a 53 MHz bunch spacing.

summary.plain: A rapid-cycling ring 474 metres around that takes protons to 8 billion electronvolts. It feeds the Booster neutrino beam and the rest of the Fermilab chain.
summary.technical: 474 m circumference rapid-cycling synchrotron running at 15 Hz, accelerating protons from 400 MeV to 8 GeV kinetic energy (8.89 GeV/c) for the BNB and for injection into the Recycler and Main Injector.
